thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_note: C1: v2.1 6.2 escalates a deviation over 2 km, but the organisers' sample DISP-001 (4.3 km) expects an AI partial refund. Not applied until Ryde confirms; flip to true to apply 6.2 as written.

traffic_justification_types.normalisation: upper-case; spaces and hyphens become underscores; then an exact match
traffic_justification_types.note: C18: the TRAFFIC_ADVISORY types the data uses (the corpus vocabulary and LTA DataMall's traffic-incident types) mapped onto v2.1 1.1's 'traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion'. Any other type (for example NONE, KERB_RESTRICTION, TRAFFIC_FLOW, WEATHER, MISC) does not justify a reroute.

integrity.note: POL-NS-08(b) makes a gap longer than 120 s inside the waiting window a policy-level impairment. A schema-level GPS_GAP tag must not, on its own, cap confidence below the 0.70 floor, or the half of POL-NS-08(b) that permits a ruling on a short gap can never operate; the pre-pass therefore grades the tag by the gap's length and position, measured from the trace itself, reading this block rather than a fixed table; the other weights are the version-1 pre-pass table moved here unchanged, so that every weight the pre-pass applies is read from policy. A fix with no reported horizontal accuracy is treated as of unknown accuracy for POL-NS-02 and is neither counted nor excluded by the 25 m filter.

clauses.title: The driver must inform the rider of a deviation
clauses.rule: A driver may reroute from the recommended route in response to real-time traffic, a road closure or congestion, but must inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. A brief reason is enough. Where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is agreed. A verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established (POL-GEN-26).
clauses.notes: Tribunal's reading where v2.1 is silent or ambiguous; to be confirmed with Ryde. C11: the records carry no call recordings.
clauses.sources: [Source] Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1 (effective 2026-01-01), released to the Digital Native track on 2026-10-13, Sections 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4

clauses.title: Measuring the deviation
clauses.rule: The deviation distance is the actual route distance minus the recommended route distance, in km: trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km, the platform's recorded distances. The GPS trace shows which route was taken and when; it is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length. A deviation of 1.0 km or less is within tolerance. Where either recorded distance is missing or impaired, the deviation cannot be established (POL-GEN-26).
clauses.notes: v2.1 1.4 formula; the 1 km tolerance is v2.1 1.3's. Tribunal's reading where v2.1 is silent or ambiguous; to be confirmed with Ryde. C17: the recorded distances, as DISP-001 uses them (24.8 - 20.5 = 4.3 km); DISP-001's 16-fix trace measures only 20.75 km and would give 0.85 km.
clauses.sources: [Source] Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1 (effective 2026-01-01), released to the Digital Native track on 2026-10-13, Sections 1.3 and 1.4

clauses.title: Traffic justification
clauses.rule: A reroute is traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure: a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. A driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute.
clauses.notes: Tribunal's reading where v2.1 is silent or ambiguous; to be confirmed with Ryde. v2.1 1.4 says traffic justification is verified via historical traffic API data; the TRAFFIC_ADVISORY artifact is that data in this schema.
clauses.sources: [Source] Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1 (effective 2026-01-01), released to the Digital Native track on 2026-10-13, Section 1.4

clauses.title: Refund matrix
clauses.rule: Exactly one row applies. (a) Traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km: no refund (NO_ACTION). (b) Traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km: refund of the excess distance fare (PARTIAL_REFUND). (c) Traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation 1 km or less: no refund, within tolerance (NO_ACTION). (d) Not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km: refund of the excess distance fare in full (PARTIAL_REFUND). (e) Not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less: no refund, within tolerance (NO_ACTION). The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent. A case that fits no row (for example, informed but the rider objected) is escalated under POL-GEN-26.
clauses.notes: Tribunal's reading where v2.1 is silent or ambiguous; to be confirmed with Ryde. C3: no surge on the excess distance fare (DISP-001: 4.3 x 0.80 = 3.44). C5: rows (b) and (d) both pay the whole excess distance fare; 'partial' and 'full' in v2.1 1.3 are read as describing the trip fare and the excess distance fare respectively. Ruling label PARTIAL_REFUND, because neither returns the whole trip fare.
clauses.sources: [Source] Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1 (effective 2026-01-01), released to the Digital Native track on 2026-10-13, Section 1.3

clauses.title: Who decides a route deviation
clauses.rule: The AI ruling on a route deviation stands only where POL-GEN-22 allows it and its confidence is 0.80 or more; otherwise the case is escalated. v2.1 6.2 also requires the deviation to be 2 km or less; that limb is held in route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied and is applied only when that field is true.
clauses.notes: Tribunal's reading where v2.1 is silent or ambiguous; to be confirmed with Ryde. C1: 6.2's 2 km limb conflicts with DISP-001; pending Ryde's answer.
clauses.sources: [Source] Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1 (effective 2026-01-01), released to the Digital Native track on 2026-10-13, Section 6.2
